name: Mixed Cystic Lymphatic Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Lymphatic Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of soft, compressible, non-tender subcutaneous or deep tissue masses with cystic components
MRI or ultrasound demonstrating multiloculated cystic lesions with both macrocystic and microcystic components
Histological confirmation showing dilated lymphatic channels lined by endothelial cells
Exclusion of venous malformations or other vascular anomalies by imaging

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical presentation plus imaging findings consistent with mixed cystic lymphatic malformation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Histopathology is confirmatory but not always required if imaging and clinical features are definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiloculated cystic masses with mixed macro- and microcystic components
searchTerms: cystic masses with mixed large and small cysts
complex cystic growths with varied cyst sizes

pathognomonic.symptomName: Progressive swelling of affected soft tissues
pathognomonic.notes: May cause functional impairment depending on location
Useful clinical sign in superficial lesions
searchTerms: cystic lesions that light up when illuminated

common.symptomName: Localized pain or tenderness due to cyst expansion or hemorrhage
common.notes: Often intermittent and related to cyst size changes
searchTerms: localized pain from cyst growth or bleeding

common.symptomName: Recurrent episodes of inflammation or infection within cystic spaces
common.notes: May present with erythema and warmth over lesion
searchTerms: repeated inflammation or infections in cysts

common.symptomName: Functional limitation or restricted range of motion in adjacent joints
common.notes: Due to mass effect or fibrosis
searchTerms: restricted range of motion from cysts

common.symptomName: Skin discoloration or overlying venous prominence
common.notes: May be present in superficial lesions
searchTerms: skin color changes with visible veins

occasional.symptomName: Hemorrhage into cystic spaces causing sudden swelling
occasional.notes: May cause acute pain and rapid enlargement
searchTerms: sudden swelling from bleeding into cysts

occasional.notes: May result in paresthesia or vascular compromise
searchTerms: pressure on nearby nerves and vessels

occasional.symptomName: Lymphorrhea or leakage of lymphatic fluid

searchTerms: fluid buildup in limb from lymph blockage

rare.symptomName: Airway obstruction due to cervical or mediastinal involvement
searchTerms: airway blockage from neck or chest masses
breathing difficulty due to cervical or mediastinal involvement

rare.symptomName: Spontaneous rupture of cystic lesions with fluid extravasation
rare.notes: May lead to local inflammation or infection
searchTerms: spontaneous cyst rupture with fluid leakage

rare.notes: Very rare but reported in literature

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; inflammatory markers may be elevated during infection
Lymphatic fluid analysis showing proteinaceous content if aspirated
imaging: Ultrasound showing multiloculated cystic lesions with septations
MRI demonstrating mixed macro- and microcystic lymphatic malformation with characteristic signal intensities
CT scan may be used to assess extent and involvement of deep structures
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified; sporadic cases predominate
Some associations with somatic mutations in PIK3CA pathway in complex lymphatic anomalies
other: Histopathology showing dilated lymphatic channels lined by endothelial cells
Immunohistochemistry positive for lymphatic endothelial markers such as D2-40 (podoplanin)

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of multiloculated cystic architecture typical of lymphatic malformations
Mixed vascular components including capillary and venous elements
More complex vascular flow patterns on Doppler imaging
Often associated with cutaneous vascular stains
Usually presents in the neck region
Lacks microcystic components seen in mixed cystic lymphatic malformations

redFlags: Rapid enlargement of lesion with pain or erythema indicating infection or hemorrhage
Airway compromise in cervical or mediastinal lesions
Neurological deficits due to nerve compression
references: Wassef M, Blei F, Adams D, et al. Vascular Anomalies Classification: Recommendations From the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015;136(1):e203-e214.
